notes.title: Clockwork Ambrosia Development Update, Spring 2025
notes.notes:
Hey there everyone! I’m Lucy, our marketing manager here at OI Games. As of recently and looking forward, I’ll be the one keeping you updated about our projects at OI Games, including Clockwork Ambrosia! So let me catch you up to speed on Clockwork Ambrosia, share some big news for the future, and tell you a story about one of our early bosses, EIK0!

[previewyoutube=Szl4VPaBVdg;full][/previewyoutube]

First and foremost, we’re moving Clockwork Ambrosia’s release date. Although narrowing the game’s scope is important for creating a balanced player experience, the development team doesn’t want to compromise the overall experience. So they’re going to take a little bit more time, and our new target is November 2025.

But I am here to follow up that potentially sad news with potentially fun news! Development has recently completed our alpha phase, and we are now planning to start a public play test in the coming months! There will be plenty of enemies to tackle, bosses to battle, and weapon mods to mix and match to do the job! Plus I’ve got to say, get ready. I’ve been lucky enough to get my hands on internal testing versions, and it’s truly something special. I’ve put my reps in against EIK0 and I can’t wait to see how you all take her on!

If you aren’t already a subscriber to my new fantastic newsletter, head on over to [url=https://oigames.substack.com]https://oigames.substack.com[/url] and sign up so that you don’t miss out on future play test announcements!

Now on to the rest of our [strike]show[/strike] letter!

[h1]Boss Fight Origins: EIK0, The Baluster Engine[/h1]
Originally EIK0 started off similar to the shield-wielding “Flat-iron” enemies that can be found around the Aqua Baluster, but our developers wanted something that was more than just a big enemy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/e55a884e428252bfcd00dffe4cfc83249fbdb414.png[/img]

The Aqua Baluster is a massive piece of technology on the island, dredging up water from the sunken ruins below. To power all of this, the Baluster needed an engine, and that was where the team stumbled upon the idea of “what if the engine was the boss?” Separately from that, the idea of oozes infesting the tower was also on the mind, leading enemy developer, Ian Clark, to bring the two ideas together and create the first rendition we would recognize as EIK0.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/fa2b8a17a007ce2294f2e06227ced4ae768415f0.png[/img]

Ian moved forward with the idea of the ooze-infused engine, working with our artist, Maciej Kuczyński, to develop a look for our ooze-filled, corrupted machine. Adding ooze arms to a cinderblock was straightforward, but they needed to also work with the attack animations. Here’s the example he sent Maciej.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/202221d8cf2c7585af325bb6ebe8c08b995572bc.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/acb751712c4b5ad8a5e2a65e140676bed7136922.png[/img]

EIK0 really started to take shape and develop into the form you see today. Now the question was “how does an engine fight?”

From there Ian wanted to create a fun dynamic, something beyond a static sprite shooting lasers at you. The ooze inside is not intentionally fighting Iris, so how would it fight? With that mindset, all of EIK0’s attacks were themed around the idea of “thrashing around” in one form or another.

“Iris was just looking to figure out why the engine wasn’t working," Ian admitted. "Then she gets trapped in a room with an engine possessed by a raging bull.”

With that framework, the focus was on attacks that made sense but offer a frantic challenge that keeps you moving. By the nature of what they are, they aren’t targeted at Iris, so the attacks were designed to be “chaotic coincidences.” They were tempered down for more consistency, but that was the starting point.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/d423acaeec816861bea297bcc0b69109b400b23e.png[/img]

Now you may be wondering, what does EIK0 stand for? Well, it was actually originally named “ICK0”.

“It was a portmanteau of Ian’s name, and his home state of Oklahoma," Michael, Clockwork Ambrosia's producer, relates. This worked when I was the one implementing the boss. But when I stepped away from development, it became Ian’s baby, and I think it made him uncomfortable to have it named after him so directly.”

After that, the name shifted to EIK0, a pet name from the engineer who created the engine based on the existing model number in-universe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/47a5e4f797e61e7f2ab3378f3c11f46f9151633e.png[/img]

That’s all this time, but you can look forward to more Clockwork Ambrosia peeks as we approach the playtest beta and launch. Keep an eye out for further updates from the newsletter so you’re notified as soon as playtesting begins: [url=https://oigames.substack.com]https://oigames.substack.com[/url] 

‘Til next time!

- Lucy

[h1]Major Changes [/h1]
[h2]Control Improvements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/1ddc8fec1bcbcda214530041cb28334da024e3e1.png[/img]
[b]Selection functionality is now more intuitive.[/b]
Swapping party members, selecting party members in menus, and scrolling through quest logs now behave more consistently in terms of left/right buttons. If you customized your keybindings, you may want to double-check your settings to avoid confusion with the new functionality.

[h2]Campaign Improvements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/11a4df460c5c02bbe6b7e605002dada493c64b48.png[/img]
[b]Several quality of life adjustments to the campaign.[/b]
A few visual enhancements are just the beginning of improvements we've made to the campaign and that includes the demo. Overall, we continue to seek ways to make the campaign smoother for players to experience!

[h2]New Save UI[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/66d38a8adf317463a90eb5f4696dec67a38562c1.png[/img]
[b]New look and syntax for save files.[/b]
The save menu has a new look, which prevents the muddled text from appearing once players got to higher numbers of save slots. In general, it's easier to read, and the save file naming convention makes it more clear which campaign you're in and where.

[h2]Characters[/h2]
[h3]Tali[/h3][list]
[*]Tier 1-3 Wand MP penalties reduced. This also ensures Tali can cast Volatile Spray with a full MP bar at Level 3, even when using the wand.
 
[/list][h2]Demo[/h2][list]
[*]Guhar: Improved overworld map scene
[*]Emerald Woods: Improved miniboss scene and removed a log from the player's natural path

[/list][h2]UI/UX[/h2][list]
[*]Adjusted some of the behaviors for selecting characters in the menu, swapping party members, and scrolling up and down in the quest log to better standardize the experience across keyboard and controller players. Note: It is recommended for players to reset their bindings to default or re-bind their desired keys again to ensure consistent and most up-to-date behavior given the internal changes.
[*] Save file UI has a slightly new look, showing more save slots at once, and with slightly more descriptive names. This also addresses a bug where save slots would render incorrectly if the current save slot was in the double-digits. Older saves may still render incorrectly, but as you continue play, over time it should look correct. To trigger the updated naming convention, simply interact with a campfire. Note that as a result of this change, background images are no longer shown in save slots.
[*]Animations on status effect applications/removal will no longer play if the Battle State Animations option is set to "Off" in the Graphics options
[*]The Reforging tutorial now has an icon
[*]The text display formatting for skill costs have been standardized

[/list][h2]Credits[/h2][list]
[*]Icon artist credits for A-Ravlik and Rexard are now attributed to Olekzandr Zahorulko
[*]Icon artist credits for lightUP is now attributed to Juliano Ferreria de Lima

[/list][h2]Bug Fixes[/h2][list]
[*]Fixed a bug where the Windows taskbar icon for the game was not displaying properly[/list]

Welcome, Tower runners! The day has come, at last, to release our definitive content update for Tower Song. We are beside ourselves (and a bit upside down, if we're being honest) to share this update with everyone, so let's get into it!

[h1]What's New in v1.0[/h1]
[h2]New Player Character: Ezoan the Technomancer[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/aca8f59da0164c5cc7ff3c80f0e504470c037733.png[/img]
[b]Players can now complete the campaign as the Technomancer Ezoan.[/b]
Ezoan is a hybrid magus who swaps between attack modes; he can tank, support, or just obliterate foes. Ezoan comes with a high skill ceiling that rewards power plays and thoughtful equipment selection.
[list]
[*] Choose Techlance to master the battlefield, spending MP to scorch foes, support allies, and lock down key targets with Time Stop. Spells generate gravity, which...
[*] Choose Exosuit to pulverize enemies with Gravity-powered abilities that can turn the tide of battle. The exosuit's powers generates Mana, which... well, see above![/list]

[h2]New Dungeon: Lharif's Doom[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/709f0293dd72538fe333f2c873431ba430230f8d.png[/img]
[b]Unlock mysteries in a brand new dungeon quest.[/b]
Lharif was a master turrologist and possibly a mad scientist. For decades, he hid away in his strange laboratory on the coast of eastern Kidonia. Legend says he perished there, the victim of his own experiments. Players can solve his riddles to uncover the truth of his tale and unlock brand new crafting recipes!

[h2]Character Reworks[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/1d02886333295b7bf5802c1dfce564f3b184422b.png[/img]
[b]Character skills have been re-balanced.[/b]
Early Access afforded us plenty of playtesting feedback about character design and balance, so just about every character has received some kind of update in v1.0. Kiran, for example, now builds into spells by generating mana through attacks and taunts, while Porphry has been re-tuned around her ability to both inflict terrible Wounds as well as soak damage for her team.

[h2]Combat Enhancements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/5d4e556ae99efbe6a5acd95054a1362abd26f389.png[/img]
[b]Dodge and Regen mechanics are updated; also new enemies![/b]
We added some new enemies to contend with, particularly in the middle chapter that could sometimes drag. Overall, combat has been touched up, and encounters have been tweaked to better support keyboard and mouse players.

[h2]Campaign Enhancements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/b9b3e6001f3aa731614471f7558246ccbf7d82cd.png[/img]
[b]We've tightened up the graphics on level 3, and we've dropped some loot.[/b]
There are new crafting recipes, new treasures, and new encounters to find! We've also fleshed out the game with wildlife, more NPCs, and improved environment designs. Tower Song has never looked so good!

[h2]Steam Deck and macOS Performance Enhancements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/15f0e60f7e7f561500ad656fce54b80986cffcb0.png[/img]
[b]New graphics settings to achieve solid FPS for Steam Deck and macOS players.[/b]
Steam Deck has long been our favorite way to play Tower Song, but we've always wanted it to perform better on macOS as well. We've made a ton of improvements under the hood, and players can tweak more graphics settings in the Options menu to get the balance they want.

[h1]About the Tower Song Soundtrack[/h1]
Alongside this v1.0 update, we have also updated the Tower Song soundtrack with the Extended tracks! This includes a new final boss theme, as well the full album of Will Aleshire tracks used in the game. 

You can purchase the soundtrack standalone or bundled with Tower Song for a discount!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2757790/Tower_Song_Soundtrack/

[h1]About Tower Song[/h1]
Tower Song is a compelling turn-based RPG that melds the classic JRPG and CRPG genres of the 1990’s into a unique mixture of deliberate turn-based combat and colorful, pixel-art worlds.

Players choose from multiple heroes to complete Tower Song's engaging 10-hour campaign. Each hero is equipped with unique battle mechanics, can explore otherwise unreachable areas of the world, and has a unique perspective on the main quest storyline. To succeed, players will also have to recruit deadly sniper Solace, magical swordsman Kiran and master of the elements Akeno. These Mana Knights will join forces to delve into the harrowing depths of the eldritch Towers and fight across the overgrown forests of Guhar and the desert expanse of Kidonia to liberate their allies from a terrible naga invasion.

[h1]Feedback, Support, and Future Updates[/h1]
Would you like to get in touch? Head on over to the Steam community forums or find us on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/vQHjYYawEt]Discord[/url]! Leave us feedback, suggestions, or report any problems you are having with the game. We will do our best to respond, but we promise we read everything sent our way.

[h1]What's Next[/h1]
We are already hard at work on our next titles. Already, we can announce our partnership with our studio co-op, Realmsoft, to publish their next title, a Megavania tour de force called Clockwork Ambrosia. Internally, we've also begun working on our next title, and we can't wait to share that with you as well. 

If you don't want to miss news about Tower Song, Clockwork Ambrosia, or Omega Intertainment updates, just joining our mailing list: [url=https://oigames.substack.com]https://oigames.substack.com[/url]

[h1]Thank You![/h1]
We make games for you to play them, and so many of you have already shared your experiences with us. From the bottom of our hearts, we wish you a warm thank you - and if you did join us in Early Access, please drop us a message for a special gift!

For everyone else, we hope you enjoy Tower Song as much as we've enjoyed creating it.

[h1]Complete Patch Notes[/h1]
Read on for a full list of changes made in this patch, both big and small!

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[h3]New Player Character: Ezoan the Technomancer[/h3][list]
[*] Play through the game as the Technomancer, Ezoan.
[*] Ezoan has been updated since the Prologue preview; his kit is now more "build and spend", focused on generating gravity through spells to deliver high value exosuit moves. 

[/list][h3]New Dungeon: Lharif's Doom[/h3][list]
[*] Obtain a new side quest in Qadam during Chapter 5
[*] Complete the new dungeon to obtain new legendary items
[*] Defeat a challenging new boss - or unlock its true secret

[/list][h3]Character Reworks[/h3][list]
[*] Akeno generates SP with his Blade of Elements and now spends SP to cast higher value spells.
[*] Kiran has been totally reworked; he now starts battle with zero MP and must build into his skills. He has new Damage-based abilities to compliment his Magic, and his Magic spells are generally more accessible. Most of his abilities have been tuned (details below), and he has several all-new abilities.
[*] Neat's finishers now gain extra effects with higher combos.
[*] Porphry is undergoing a significant rework still - look forward to our first major patch in the near future!
[*] Solace's Mana Battery and Overwatch have been reworked to allow Solace to gain and provide more direct benefit while using them.
[*] Tali can now give Jiji access to a new attack move.
[*] The Legionnaires Fred and Hudson now begin Chapter 6 with a new skill

[/list][h3]Combat Enhancements[/h3][list]
[*] New Enemy: Runner Queen - A terror in the desert who leads her swarm to eviscerate prey.
[*] New Enemy: Busaiya - A new look for the potted ephemera in the Fire Tower.
[*] Dodge (previously Evasion) and Regen are now stacking states like Wound.
[*] Enemy Types: All enemies are assigned a type, which grants them Defense bonuses and other resistances. These are viewable in battle. Enemies don't otherwise resist or absorb damage behind the scenes, unless buffed/debuffed during combat.

[/list][h3]Campaign Enhancements[/h3][list]
[*] There are more battles to conquer, items to craft, and loot to find!
[*] The world has come to life with more animation, characters, wildlife and unique character art for villagers
[*] The Guhar overworld map has been greatly improved, visually
[*] Most Fire Tower stages have been revisited with updated appearances and layouts
[*] The camera perspective has been adjusted for dungeons and other key moments to enhance the mood
[*] Flavor text has been added to objects throughout the game

[/list][h3]Performance Enhancements[/h3][list]
[*] We have added support for more international keyboards, such as French
[*] Map and combat performance has been improved across the game for all platforms.
[*] Steam Deck users can select the Performance Graphics preset to enjoy 60 FPS throughout the game (with some exceptions during scene loads or combat turns).
[*] Uers can also select a Minimal Graphics preset to achieve better performance on lower spec systems.
[/list]
[h2]Warning: The below details may contain minor plot spoilers.[/h2]

[h2]Achievements[/h2][list]
[*] 'So Much Damage' Achievement now requires 500 damage instead of 150

[h2]Characters[/h2]
[h3]Akeno[/h3][list]
[*] New cut-scene portrait!
[*] Blades and Katanas grant the same damage bonus, but Katana now grants MP
[*] Blade of Elements skills generate SP.

[*] Phoenix Song: MP no longer required to cast. SP required to cast.
[*] Soothe: Bonus spirit now grants Regen +2.

[/list][h3]Hudson[/h3][list]
[*] Live Loadout: Remove cooldown; while switching weapons, players now see the current ammo count.

[/list][h3]Fred[/h3][list]
[*] Scythe no longer grants HP regen but instead a static HP bonus

[/list][h3]Jiji[/h3][list]
[*] New Ability - Lunar Strike: A single-target ability that deals bonus damage.
[*] Ward is now free, but has a 1-turn cooldown. It is no longer automatically cast on Tali.

[/list][h3]Kiran[/h3][list]
[*] New Ability - Determination: Passive talent that grants Kiran a Defense bonus based on his missing health.
[*] New Ability - Eldritch Strike: Deal critical Slashing Damage to target.

[*] New Ability - Knight Run: Cleanse party and grant immunity to negative states for 3 turns.

[*] Mana Strike: Now a purely Magic skill.
[*] Matyr: Now a free action.
[*] Quantum Soul: MP restoration bonus reduced to 10.
[*] Siphon Strike: Damage reduced; MP gain increased.
[*] Soulchained Shock: MP cost reduced
[*] Spell Breaker: MP cost reduced
[*] Steel Hurricane: Now costs MP.

[/list][h3]Neat[/h3][list]
[*] No longer sees invalid moves in his skill list during combat.

[*] Sogruni War Cry: Skill removed.

[/list][h3]Solace[/h3][list]
[*] Hit points increased

[*] Sniper Rifle: Damage increased
[*] Burst Fire damage reduced
[*] First Aid grants a turn to a revived ally if an ally was revived
[*] Explosive Grenade: Damage increased
[*] Knight's Aid: Now grants Regen +4.

[*] Overwatch: Damage bonus now scales from Solace's Damage, not the target's; Solace can no longer mark multiple enemies by using Overwatch twice in a row; Solace now visibly fires on her ally's target
[*] Smoke Grenade: Now grants Dodge +3.

[/list][h3]Tali[/h3][list]
[*] Staves now grant HP instead of MP; wands now come with an MP penalty
[*] Commune no longer grants MP to the party, only to Tali and Jiji

[*] Tarot Pull: Tali can no longer pull the same card twice at once
[*] Void Kill damage reduced and MP cost increased.

[/list][h2]Combat[/h2]
[h3]General[/h3][list]
[*] Combat difficulty has been tuned across the board; enemies have been added to trivial fights and removed from harder fights. Some new encounters have been added to better introduce enemy mechanics; and others are now easier to avoid entirely.

notes.title: Developer Blog: The 4x4 Design of Tower Song
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=Wy46elePmrM;full][/previewyoutube]

(This post is a text version of the above video.)

I have a problem: I really like coming up with RPG character designs. 

Tower Song features four heroes for players to choose from as their point of view character. Each character comes with their own unique class design, dialogue, and quest rewards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/9b9739bd208acf1f440738bb8ca0e3e4044e46f1.png[/img]

Tali is a spellcaster, so while she uses mana points, she doesn’t really have a spell list - instead she pulls Tarot cards, each of which grants her a different spell. Of course, she also fights with Jiji, who is himself a party member. In the field, Jiji can sneak into tiny spaces, finding treasure or unlocking doors from the other side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/122ce2e28bfeeec843822320bdc994fd80373440.png[/img]

Neat is the ultimate tempo fighter; each skill he has adjusts his Combo Stage, meanwhile; depending on the stage, he can access different moves. So he has an entirely different moveset each turn, depending on what you are doing. In the field, he can walk Song-addled victims through meditation techniques, allowing the party to pass into areas without violence.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/be2b83e904ff61e62251482ac45e3e21c750d322.png[/img]

Porphry is fury, a mix between a berserker and a fighter. Her skills generate Trance, which, like Neat, can change what skills she has access to. But she can also lower her Trance; why do this? Well once her Trance gets high enough, she goes into a berserker rage, and players lose control of her. In the field, she can break down weakened walls or obstacles, opening up new areas to explore.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/a9226e4b6a3e1f5d48fe367d84e54800ab38cc05.png[/img]

Ezoan is a fun hybrid spellcaster and fighter; he casts spells like others, but he also drives an exosuit; the exosuit is powered by gravity, which he generates by casting spells. In the field, he can hack exosuits, moving them or just exposing them to the player for loot.

All of this is driven by a compulsion for me to design RPG characters; as many as I have ideas for, usually, and for whatever reason, I am never short on those.

You might think this is a boon, and it is certainly a more helpful problem than having no ideas at all. Let me give you a little context though.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/888a14cdac61f419e80610eb9b30fa8035cefc8e.png[/img]

The original RPG Maker 2000 game had 8 members in the main cast. It was also quite a bit longer than Tower Song, with a main quest running around 20 hours and a bunch of side quest content bringing it to about 30 or 40 hours to 100%. If 8 sounds maybe reasonable, however, you should also know I included an additional 9 hirable mercenaries as well. They didn’t have any speaking lines and some of them couldn’t hit the level cap, but, you know, that’s just a lot of characters. Too many, some might say. (Meaning myself.)

Even the original Tower Song prototype had this problem, featuring 7 characters with a main quest clocking in only around 2 hours.

I knew Tower Song would need to rein it in and be more focused. The harder option - increasing the game’s length - was out of the question. Not only did I not want to ask players to commit to another 40-hour long RPG, I also wasn’t going to have the art budget to create a game of that scope.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/efd64aa7dd00194ce06e2e37e60edf086b9cc77e.png[/img]

The solution seemed genius: narrow down the prototype’s cast to 3 main characters and allow the player to choose their own main character from the remaining four. We could then commit our resources to a single main quest line (and the handful of biomes that went with it), while still being able to play around with all of the class designs we wanted to.

One thing I did not want, however, was a silent protagonist. Nor should their lines simply be inserted into longer cut-scenes as “fill in the blank” asides. No, I felt strongly that the player’s character (let’s call them the “hero”) should have their own goals, motivations, and personalities - and be vocal about it. 

All of this, of course, created a single game of reasonable scope that was then multiplied into four games, with a perhaps less reasonable scope! Everything we did, had to be done four times. 

Bug testing: many bugs only appeared for one or two heroes, necessitating campaign playthroughs with all four characters in order to certify a build.

Combat balance: getting encounters, particularly the “story bosses”, to feel just right in combat meant they had to feel right for each potential party. A trivial fight for one party composition could be near impossible with another.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/d2598bd876981dbaa95050bae706252e31ca8b7c.png[/img]

Side quests: if we’re adding a side quest with a unique reward for one hero, at the very least, four rewards had to be designed - one for each. To make side content feel truly special, though, we also wanted areas and encounters unique to a hero - which then meant we had to design four times as many.

Storyline: While some cut-scenes do not really involve the hero and the dialogue is the same for all four, allowing each hero to bring their own personality to bear often meant cut-scenes were so driven by character that there was no option except to write the scene four different times.

Class design: This was the whole point, so you can believe we had four different designs. 

So did it work out?

Well, yes, I think so!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/d4a1b76ed0be36aad0c704bb5ac974e2ab3acb45.png[/img]

The game certainly took longer to developer than I anticipated, but the result is something special. Although the outcome of the main story does not change, each hero in Tower Song is otherwise a unique experience. Whether you play it once, or four times, your choice is rewarded. You even learn about the world just a little differently depending on your hero and the perspective they bring; party builds and battles also play out differently, due to the totally different class designs.

So will we do it again? Not sure! It’s a lot of work. But I did learn a valuable lesson about scope, all the same. Maybe that’s progress for me. A sign of progress.

That’s good, right?

See you next time.

(All of this is a lie, of course, because we still found cause to add another two playable characters into the game’s final chapter. Once an addict, always an addict, I suppose.)

notes.title: Dev Blog: Achieving "Content Complete" for Tower Song
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=eoRgWAhSGi8;full][/previewyoutube]

(This is the text version of our YouTube developer blog, linked above.)

For Tower Song, the term “content complete” means, primarily, that all four of the main player characters are implemented in terms of storyline and combat mechanics. Additionally, it means the implementation of additional side content not originally planned when we launched Early Access back in November. 

One of the largest and, for us, most successful pieces of new side content was the addition of an entirely new dungeon in the game. While not as long as the Tower runs in the main quest, it’s an entirely unique experience all the same. We think players will have a great time exploring its secrets!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/9b9739bd208acf1f440738bb8ca0e3e4044e46f1.png[/img]

We launched Early Access with two playable characters - the witch and her familiar, Tali & Jiji, and the street fighter, Neat - and had plans to implement two more: the berserker, Porphry (who went live in February), and the technomancer, Ezoan.

Getting the class designs for each of the main characters right was a huge priority for the team. From the beginning, combat in Tower Song was meant to be a standout feature for the game, something we felt could distinguish us in an otherwise crowded market. The biggest example of this is our standalone encounter design: every battle in the game is a unique assortment of monsters (and often, the monsters are unique themselves). These encounters are tuned to present a range of challenges to the player, from basic “teaching” battles to fights so dangerous that players are within only 1 or 2 turns from total party knockout at any given moment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/7739b2731d47df8e9c4610b09ecdc0c1be96106d.png[/img]

Back to Early Access and player feedback - several players suggested that we give Jiji players the ability to send Jiji exploring on his own, into small caves or other spaces. We liked this idea so much, we decided to put it in the game! Of course, Tower Song being what it is, everything comes in fours - so we ended up doing the same thing for each of the main characters: Neat can move “Song-addled” victims out of the way; Porphry can bust down doors or smash obstacles; Ezoan can hack ancient exosuits. All of them will find loot unique to their run and even get into a few encounters unique to their paths as well. (Loot, by the way, turned out to be a missed opportunity in the Early Access version. We added a lot more of it over the course of Early Access!)

We also decided to revamp the legendary item system as well. In Early Access, players could obtain legendary items by completing fairly straight forward side quests. This ultimately did not feel interesting or rewarding enough for us, so instead legendary items became multi-step crafting recipes that each hero could unlock by finding materials unique to their playthrough.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/41fd0d4fea1eb759ce590a1b2dbd16e1843b0148.png[/img]

Last but not least, let’s say a few words about the Steam Deck. This was a target platform for us from the beginning; Tower Song was just perfect for it. Fortunately, our engine choice (RPG Maker) made this easy. Unfortunately, the custom code we ran to make Tower Song what it is made the actual Steam Deck performance not always so great. So our programmer, Ishin Iwasaki, worked very hard to get Steam Deck running at a near constant 60-fps - a huge achievement we are very excited to include.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/11aa6cbf02138ef15068520b228594af40b4461b.png[/img]

What is next for Omega Intertainment? I often wonder, as I play great indie games, if the studio is a one-off or if this new game is just the beginning. So, while it’s too early to get into specifics, I am also happy to say that we are already hard at work on our next game, which we hope players will get their first look at in 2025!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/4d59e8362521b393b87186a4e8538ec9674435c7.png[/img]

In the meantime, Tower Song 1.0 is nearly here. Our final release date is June 20 2024! Wishlist (or buy) Tower Song on Steam today, and make sure you subscribe to our [url=https://oigames.substack.com]newsletter [/url]for more updates like this in the future!

notes.title: Tower Song Content Update #1: The Fury
notes.notes:
Greetings Tower runners; welcome to the first Early Access content patch for Tower Song! This update includes our first new player character, Porphry the Fury! Plus, better controller support, totally revamped accessories and loot, and much, [b]much[/b] more! Read on for details - and don't forget to leave us a review with your honest opinion! It means the world to us!

As always, a big thank you to our fans and players for your diligence in finding and reporting these problems to our development team! Props to the following bug hunters this go round:[list]
[*]Tortalius
[*]Vorticia[/list]
Want to leave us feedback for this patch or the game in general? Head on over to [url=https://www.omegaintertainment.com/feedback]feedback[/url] or find us on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/vQHjYYawEt]Discord[/url]! 

If you don't want to miss future Tower Song updates, just joining our mailing list: [url=https://oigames.substack.com]https://oigames.substack.com[/url]

[h1]Major Changes [/h1]

[h2]New Player Character: Porphry the Fury[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/be2b83e904ff61e62251482ac45e3e21c750d322.png[/img]
[b]Players can now complete the campaign as the Fury, Porphry.[/b]
Porphry is a true terror on the battlefield, and her campaign release comes with a completely reworked skillset from the original preview dungeon. Porphry engages in battle with her Battle Trance, a gauge that measures her dedication to the task at hand. Build her Trance to unlock truly devastating skills, but beware! If Porphry's Trance ever hits the threshold, she will temporarily loose control and go into a Berserker Rage, attacking a random target for many turns until the target - or Porphry - falls!

[h2]New Exploration Abilities[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/7739b2731d47df8e9c4610b09ecdc0c1be96106d.png[/img]
[b]Each player character can access new areas with unique abilities.[/b]
Squeeze into caves with Jiji, smash through barriers with Porphry, or talk down Song-addled victims with Neat! Players can access unique, secret areas with their player character and find loot - and fight bosses! - not reachable with other characters.

[h2]Loot Revamp[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/d2598bd876981dbaa95050bae706252e31ca8b7c.png[/img]
[b]Many more treasures to find, and many equipments overhauled.[/b]
We all love loot! Players can now find many more items and brand-new armors and accessories scattered throughout the world, and the content of many existing treasures has been upgraded. There are many, many new accessories that should help players craft just the right build for their team.

[h2]Expanded Prologue Tutorial[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/c90cfb739bdb174fc4f56bdc7df69297bbdd1c74.png[/img]
[b]The Prologue is further developed with more graceful tutorials.[/b]
Solace's Tower heist section was a little under-developed, so we've expanded her adventure - along with the loot she can find. Additionally, we've taken a closer look at tutorials in the Prologue and re-worked the UI to more intuitively explain features that previously required heavy-handed tutorialization. A few tutorials will still appear so players understand the key features of Tower Song; the rest can still be found in the Guidebook in-game.

[h2]PlayStation Controller Support & More[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/a5563579f588bbb27438c132eaab750499be7fd7.png[/img]
[b]Official support for DualShock, DualSense and Nintendo-layout controllers.[/b]
We've put in a lot of work to try and make the controller experience better, since we feel Tower Song is best enjoyed with a controller. Players now see button shortcuts on-screen (disabled in Options if desired) to help them key-in to functionality. Additionally, we have added additional button shortcuts for Equipment and Mod menus (for keyboard players too!), and players now have more options to select their controller button layout (great for controllers like 8BitDo) and shoulder buttons. Let us know if you have a controller option that we didn't account for!

[h2]More Art![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/8f41701931f890d7d03d9b0f166a5beecc4e7215.png[/img]
[b]Many new art assets in-game, including cavern battlegrounds, Fire Tower environments, animations for Kiran and Akeno, and much more.[/b]
We're always seeking to improve, so we've added a lot more art to the game! We hope you enjoy!

[h1]Complete Patch Notes[/h1]

[h3]New Player Character: Porphry the Fury[/h3][list]
[*]Play through the game as the Fury, Porphry

[*]Jiji can squeeze into hard to reach places to find new treasure.

[*]Porphry can break through weak obstacles to access secret areas

[*]Many new chests have also been placed in the world with new items.
[*]Players can now craft 5 full tiers of helmets and shields.

[/list][h3]Updated Prologue & Tutorials[/h3][list]
[*]Solace's portion of the Tower Heist is now more involved and includes more loot to find.
[*]Tutorials are now less intrusive and more intuitive

[/list][h3]New Art[/h3][list]
[*]Additional environment art for the Fire Tower.
[*]New battle background art in forest and desert caves
[*]Improved animations for Kiran and Akeno's skills
[*]And much more...

[/list][h3]Improved Controller Support[/h3][list]
[*]Players can now open Equipment menu with a single button; Main Menu has been rebound to Start button
[*]Players can now open Mod menu with a single button; Dash has been rebound to trigger/L2/R2 buttons
[*]Button shortcuts are now persistently displayed on-screen. This can be disabled in Options.
[*]Options: Players can now choose their button layout (great for 8Bit Do players!)
[*]Now officially compatible with DualShock and DualSense over USB and Bluetooth. Note that Steam DS players should re-enable Steam Input to benefit from this.

[/list][h2]Characters[/h2]

Akeno's default armor upgraded to Soul Plate

[/list][h3]Ezoan[/h3][list]

[/list][h3]Hudson[/h3][list]
[*]Live Loadout: Now a free action to change weapons but does not reload
[*]Reload => Reload-out: Refills ammo for all 3 weapons
[*]Removed low value skills to make character easier to get into: Quick Draw and No One of Consequence

[/list][h3]Kiran[/h3][list]
[*]Kiran's default armor upgraded to Refined Plate
[*]Bastion: Now a Tier 3 skill
[*]Charm Attack => Muddling Strike: Now deals physical damage; no longer inflicts Cursed Armor
[*]Eldritch Blast: No longer benefits from MAG

[*]Honored Sacrifice: Now a free action that bypasses barriers but has a higher HP cost; moved to a Tier 4 skill
[*]Mana Hurricane => Steel Hurricane: Now a Physical attack; now a Tier 3 mod

Hello and welcome to Tower Song's first Early Access release! This update includes a handful of additional minor features and class tweaks, plus a true trove of bug fixes. Thanks to our fans and testers for their diligence in reporting problems to the development team!

Want to leave us feedback for this patch or the game in general? Head on over to [url=https://www.omegaintertainment.com/feedback]feedback[/url].

Now, on to the good stuff. What does Early Access Patch #1 bring us?

[h1]Major Changes[/h1]
[h2]Neat's Adjustment[/h2]
[b]Adjustment now revives (and heals) dead allies when used at Stage 4-5.[/b]
This gives Neat additional benefit for holding onto his combo for longer and gives him more options to keep his team running in prolonged fights.

[h2]Crafting for Kiran and Akeno[/h2]
[b]Players can now craft lower tier weapons for Kiran and Akeno.[/b]
This allows players to better manage their loadout for late-game parties without having to choose between underpowered equipment and costly higher tier weapons.

[h2]Regen States[/h2]
[b]Regen states now provide immunity to Wounds.[/b]
It's too easy for enemies to wound regenerating allies, and regen effects are often costly to grant party members in the first place. This adjustment gives more value to classes with regen abilities.

[h2]Stun States[/h2]
[b]Removing stun effects now allies the party member to act during the round, if they haven't acted yet.[/b]
Stun is a punishing status effect to begin with and removing stun effects is not trivial. This gives increased incentive to actively remove the effect and rewards players who do so.

[h2]Boss Fight: Siege Beast[/h2]
[b]Boss' initiative greatly reduced and reinforcements now appear in stages.[/b]
The fight was nearly impossible on Hard mode, and the addition of phased reinforcements also adds additional tension to the fight. Players are now pressured to capitalize on their opportunity to damage the boss and are not punished for being unable to manage a large enemy party.

[h2]Side Quest: Missing Miners[/h2]
[b]Finding all of the miners (dead or alive) now results in a better reward.[/b]

notes.title: Tower Song Open Beta: Final Round!
notes.notes:
As we near Tower Song's launch date, we are excited to share a nearly-completed campaign with our avid playtesters. This update includes three new playable chapters for players to experience, plus a host of balance changes, bug fixes, and quality of life updates. Thank you as always to our players who have helped us make this a better game!

Please also read on for two important notes about save files and character selection.

[h1]Campaign Content Unlocked: The Kido Desert[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/d7a573787b146ef9cf096317aed83a9510ec1cb9.png[/img]
Join Solace and her companion as they return to Solace's homeland to rescue her sister from the clutches of the Fire Tower! Unfortunately, during their absence, a terrible darkness has fallen over the land that threatens the Mana Knights and their loved ones.

Pack up your gear for the continuation of the Tower Song story, and recruit the 4th (and final) member of the party, the Elementalist, Akeno!

[h1]Save File Compatibility[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/884773fdb2c64a7319d0f76587119bd8372409b5.png[/img]
This update to the game renders all old save files unusable. While we had hoped to maintain continuity for save files for the rest of the playtest and into the full launch, this was simply impossible to do while still delivering the latest functionality we wanted.

That said, we have locked in our core engine features, so we will endeavor to maintain save file continuity going forward. This means that starting with this version of the game, save files [b]will [/b]be transferable from both Steam Playtest and the Tower Song Demo.

[h1]Character Selection: Neat Unplayable[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/f85cb61e40385029051ebca1863aadf639065310.png[/img]
To allow us to focus on quality, this update of the game only includes Tali as the playable character. We are working as hard as we can to make other characters available for launch, but we wanted to be up front about the choice for this build. As it turns out, writing, scripting and balancing an RPG for multiple characters is a lot of work! But we don't want to compromise on the quality of Neat's story just to keep him playable.

[h1]v0.16 Release Notes[/h1]
Read on for a detailed list of changes to the game.

[h2]A Note on Save Files[/h2]
[list]
[*] This beta test build is destructive towards old save files, which will not  work after updating. This is the last time we will do this, but it was necessary to get some key features to work. You should be able to skip to whatever chapter you left off on from the Chapter Select menu. Just let us know if you have any problems or concerns about this - and we are very sorry!
[*] Going forward, playtest (and demo) save files will be transferable to the main game, although we may have to provide players with one-time options to upgrade their save files if more destructive events do occur. 
[*] As such, the extra level up in the demo after the Wolf Cave has been disabled
[/list]

[h2]A Note About Character Selection[/h2]
For the time being, Tali is the only playable character, as she has been the focus of our writing and development for the beta test. Neat is still planned for 22 November. We wanted his dialogue to feel impactful and unique to his campaign, so we are still working on it!
Thus, the character select menu is temporarily disabled

[h2]New Features[/h2]

[h3]New Playable Chapter: Vistham[/h3]
[list]
[*] Solace's homeland is under attack. Team up with a new ally and save the port city of Vistham from monstrous invaders!
[*] Select "Chapter Select" from the title screen to dive right in.
[/list]

[h3]New Playable Chapter: Armin Mountains[/h3]
In order to save her homeland, Solace must lead her teams on a secret route into the capital of Kidonia, the Jewel of the Vito Coast, Qadam.

[h3]New Playable Chapter: Qadam[/h3]
Our heroes prepare for their most dangerous mission yet.

[h3]Lore/Dialogue Revamp [/h3]  
[list]
[*] Cutscenes have been revised and cleaned up for the entire game. No changes to the core plot, but a lot of jargon has been removed, and character motivations are cleaned up, while relevations and plots twists are sequenced a bit better. There is not enough change here to warrant re-playing Chapters you already completed, unless you just enjoy reading or replaying the game! That said, read on for a spoiler-filled update of major changes:
[*] SPOILERS Chapter 1 - Emerald River[list]
[*] The rest of the Mana Knights are not in prison, but simply attending to business in Qadam.
[*] Solace and the player are now here to rescue Kiran in order to get his help rescuing Solace's sister, Amara, who is trapped in Qadam's Fire Tower
[*] The player characters were all originally Mana Knights and know Kiran[/list]
[*] SPOILERS Chapter 2 - Moldlight Mines[list]
[*] A Tower Guardian is now a theoretical entity, but one Kiran is determined to pursue and interrogate.
[*] Less information about the Fire Goddess is revealed during Aomr's final conversation, and there is no longer a suggestion that she is also a Tower Guardian. Aomr appears to be one of a kind![/list]
[/list]

[h2]Combat[/h2]
[list]
[*] Enemy HP increased in Chapter 2-3 to account for increased party size
[*] Solace: Scatter Shot's Stun effect has been adjusted to Quick Stun Quick Stun only lasts for the current round, instead of two.
[*] Hudson: Fixed a bug where Live Loadout was not swapping weapons correctly.
[*] Tali & Jiji[list]

[*] Summon Familiar displays cooldown properly[/list]
[/list]

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]

[/list]

[*] New Tutorials have been added for Player Characters

[*] Upon losing an encounter, the option to change loadout has been renamed for clarity.
[/list]
  
[h2]Art Updates[/h2]

[*] Jiji's collar is now green, like our real boy's was
[*] Character biography portraits re-worked to better fit into the menu
[*] New ladder shortcut art in Kido Highway!

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/1f4aa946f5a6d502f03bfc3eba13333edff36301.png[/img]
Our game director, Michael, will play the demo and answer questions live from the audience. The core focus of this event will be the characters and story, but all questions are welcome!

Tower Song is a turn-based retro-fusion JRPG with engaging, strategy-heavy combat and multiple point-of-view characters for players to choose from!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/0a3d6aedc55712cc476185644ead56cd3e6d9ab6.gif[/img]

[*] Level up by progressing the story quest
[*] Proactively plan turns by previewing enemy's moves
[*] Customize your class skills with impactful mods
[*] Simple crafting system for player expression

[*] Traverse retro-inspired overworlds to access new areas
[*] Explore pixel-art SNES style environments
[*] Accessible difficulty modes to suit your preferences
[/list]

Players choose one of four heroes for their journey: the rampaging fury, the cosmic witch and her cat familiar, the philosophical street fighter, or the Exosuit-piloting, spell-slinging technomancer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/4839b38942690c2951cf3728de62ac106404b169.gif[/img]
Our heroes will journey overland across multiple biomes before descending into the mysterious Towers.
